topic: Mutual Fund and ETF Fees and Expenses
subtopic: ETF Premiums and Discounts to Net Asset Value
source_evidence: An ETF share is trading at a premium when its market price is higher than the NAV per share.
question: Misconception: An ETF premium is an extra fee charged by the fund whenever you buy its shares.
answer: A premium is not described here as a fee. It means the ETF’s market price is higher than its net asset value (NAV) per share. Because of this difference, a buyer may pay more than NAV, while a seller may receive more or less than NAV depending on the market price.
